2026-11-06.headline: OAuth migration endpoints and mailbox limits lead this Exchange update
2026-11-06.overview: The period delivered two substantive administrator guides: one covering OAuth authentication for Microsoft 365 Mailbox Replication Service migrations and another documenting Exchange Online message-size limits. Message Center notices also cover a policy-controlled unified inbox in new Outlook, Outlook event duplication, and custom profile-card properties planned for January 2027.
2026-11-06.adminImpact: Admins adopting OAuth-based migrations need Entra ID access, a configured migration domain, and an on-premises API application registration; the documented server scope is Exchange Server Subscription Edition or Exchange 2019 CU15 with the latest ESU, paired with Microsoft 365 commercial cloud. Mail-flow administrators can use the documented EAC and PowerShell settings while accounting for message overhead. New Outlook administrators should review policy controls for the All Accounts view. The event-duplication notice requires no action, while custom profile properties will require setup if adopted from January 2027.

keyChanges.title: OAuth authentication is documented for MRS migration endpoints
keyChanges.detail: A new Hybrid guide explains how Microsoft 365 Mailbox Replication Service can use OAuth for migrations between Microsoft 365 and on-premises Exchange. It covers Entra ID application registration and supports Exchange Server Subscription Edition or Exchange 2019 CU15 with the latest ESU, together with Microsoft 365 commercial cloud. Adoption requires Entra ID access, migration-domain configuration, and registration of the on-premises API application.

keyChanges.title: Exchange Online message-size guidance sets concrete defaults and limits
keyChanges.detail: The new mail-flow article documents 35 MB sending and 36 MB receiving defaults, configurable mailbox limits from 1 MB to 150 MB, and EAC and PowerShell configuration. It also explains how headers, encoding, attachments, and content conversion contribute to message overhead and the effective limit.

keyChanges.title: New Outlook adds a policy-controlled All Accounts inbox
keyChanges.detail: The All Accounts, or Unified Inbox, view in new Outlook for Windows lets users manage email from multiple accounts in one view without merging the underlying mailboxes. Administrators can enable or disable the feature through a policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center and control whether users can override the setting.

keyChanges.title: Outlook is rolling out event duplication
keyChanges.detail: The new Duplicate event capability lets users create an event from an existing one without re-entering its details. Microsoft says rollout began in late September 2026 and is scheduled to finish by early December 2026; the notice calls for no administrator action or compliance changes.

keyChanges.title: Profile cards will support up to 10 third-party custom properties
keyChanges.detail: Starting in January 2027, administrators will be able to add up to 10 properties from external systems to Microsoft 365 profile cards through Microsoft Graph People connectors. The feature is off by default and requires administrator setup; later updates are planned for SAP SuccessFactors and Workday support.

2026-11-09.headline: EWS deprecation drives migration of cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, Calendar Sharing
2026-11-09.overview: Exchange Online administrators face an active migration requirement for cross-tenant calendar and messaging features, while classic Outlook for Windows is scheduled for a cosmetic refresh with no workflow change.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Prioritize migration from Exchange Web Services for cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing. Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy is scheduled to replace EWS by late November 2026; the GCC rollout is paused. No administrator action is required for the upcoming classic Outlook visual changes.

keyChanges.title: Cross-tenant EWS workflows require migration
keyChanges.detail: EWS deprecation began October 1, 2026, affecting cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing. Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy will replace EWS by late November 2026. Microsoft says organizations must migrate to avoid disruption and notes that the GCC rollout is paused.

keyChanges.title: Classic Outlook receives visual updates without workflow changes
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-November 2026, classic Outlook for Windows will update icons, spacing, and alignment. A nonintrusive monthly “What’s New” dialog will inform users; Microsoft says no administrator action is needed and the changes will not replace the classic experience or alter workflows.

2026-11-11.headline: OAuth migration endpoint guidance narrows supported platforms and changes the optional claim
2026-11-11.overview: The OAuth Migration Endpoint guidance now limits supported environments from October 2026 onward to Microsoft 365 multi-tenant (WW) and on-premises Exchange Server SE, or Exchange 2019 CU15 with the October 2026 security update. It also changes the optional claim to `xms_aud_guid` and adds endpoint-testing and move-request examples.
2026-11-11.adminImpact: Administrators configuring the OAuth migration integration should verify the platform prerequisite, use `xms_aud_guid`, test the endpoint, and ensure URI host values match the migration commands.

keyChanges.title: Supported environment requirements are narrowed
keyChanges.detail: From October 2026 onward, the guidance supports Microsoft 365 multi-tenant (WW) and on-premises Exchange Server SE, or Exchange 2019 CU15 with the October 2026 security update.

keyChanges.title: OAuth configuration and validation examples changed
keyChanges.detail: The optional claim is now `xms_aud_guid`; the guidance also adds endpoint-testing and move-request examples and requires URI host values to match the migration commands.

2026-11-13.headline: Outlook mobile Copilot Chat gets refreshed Microsoft 365 design starting December
2026-11-13.overview: Microsoft is updating Copilot Chat in Outlook for iOS and Android with a more consistent Microsoft 365 design, improved chat interface, refreshed prompts, and revised navigation. Rollout is scheduled to begin in mid-December 2026 and complete by late January 2027.
2026-11-13.adminImpact: No administrator action or compliance changes are required for this update.

keyChanges.title: Copilot Chat interface refresh for Outlook mobile
keyChanges.detail: Copilot Chat in Outlook for iOS and Android will receive updated design, chat interface, prompts, and navigation. The rollout starts in mid-December 2026 and is expected to finish by late January 2027.

2026-11-02.headline: Exchange Admin API permission and response changes put app integrations on notice
2026-11-02.overview: The week’s most consequential Exchange updates affect automation rather than mailbox features. Microsoft is replacing two Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 permissions by November 2026 and changing the MailboxFolderPermission response shape in early November. New guidance also documents OAuth-authenticated hybrid migrations, while a separate article records current message-size defaults and configuration limits.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Administrators responsible for Exchange integrations should inventory applications using the affected Admin API permissions, transition them to the new permissions, obtain consent, verify RBAC roles, test, and remove the legacy permissions. They should also update consumers of MailboxFolderPermission to process the User object’s new fields. Hybrid teams evaluating OAuth migrations should confirm the documented Exchange and Entra ID prerequisites; mailbox-size changes are configuration-dependent rather than required by this update.

keyChanges.title: Admin API permissions are being replaced
keyChanges.detail: Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 will replace Exchange.ManageV2 and Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 with new permissions by November 2026. Affected applications need an updated permission grant, admin consent, RBAC verification, testing, and removal of the old permissions; Microsoft says endpoint changes are not involved.

keyChanges.title: MailboxFolderPermission will return a structured User object
keyChanges.detail: By early November 2026, the Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 MailboxFolderPermission endpoint will return User as an object containing DisplayName, Name, and PrimarySmtpAddress. Applications that expect the current response shape may need code changes to avoid errors.

keyChanges.title: OAuth migration endpoint guidance covers supported hybrid versions
keyChanges.detail: New guidance explains how Microsoft 365 Mailbox Replication Service can authenticate migrations with OAuth between Microsoft 365 and on-premises Exchange. The documented path requires Entra ID access, migration-domain configuration, and registration of an on-premises API application, and supports Exchange Server Subscription Edition or Exchange 2019 CU 15 with the latest ESU in the Microsoft 365 commercial cloud.

keyChanges.title: Message-size guidance sets 35 MB and 36 MB defaults
keyChanges.detail: The new Exchange Online article documents 35 MB sending and 36 MB receiving defaults, mailbox limits configurable from 1 to 150 MB, and EAC and PowerShell procedures. It also explains that headers, encoding, attachments, and content conversion contribute to message overhead and can reduce the effective limit.

2026-11-09.headline: EWS deprecation and new Outlook attachment defaults demand Exchange preparation
2026-11-09.overview: The most consequential changes are operational. Microsoft says EWS deprecation affects cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing from October 1, 2026, with Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy replacing EWS by late November; GCC rollout is paused. Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows will also block .msix and .msixbundle files by default in OwaMailboxPolicy starting in December 2026. Updated hybrid guidance narrows OAuth Migration Endpoint prerequisites, while separate Outlook client updates are primarily user-interface changes.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Prioritize migration for the affected cross-tenant EWS scenarios. If users need .msix or .msixbundle attachments, allow those file types in OwaMailboxPolicy before the December rollout. Hybrid administrators configuring the OAuth Migration Endpoint must use the updated supported-platform prerequisites and xms_aud_guid claim, test the endpoint, and ensure URI host values match move-request commands. No administrator action is identified for the Copilot Chat or classic Outlook visual updates.

keyChanges.title: Cross-tenant EWS scenarios must move to Cross-Tenant Access Policy
keyChanges.detail: EWS deprecation affects cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing. Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy is scheduled to replace EWS for these capabilities by late November 2026; the GCC rollout is paused, and migration guidance is available.

keyChanges.title: Outlook will block .msix and .msixbundle files by default
keyChanges.detail: Starting in December 2026, Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows will update OwaMailboxPolicy defaults to block .msix and .msixbundle file types. Organizations that use these files should allow them in policy before rollout; no action is needed otherwise.

keyChanges.title: OAuth Migration Endpoint guidance narrows supported hybrid environments
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance supports Microsoft 365 multi-tenant (WW) and on-premises Exchange Server SE from October 2026 onward, or Exchange 2019 CU15 with the October 2026 security update. It changes the optional claim to xms_aud_guid and adds endpoint-testing and move-request examples.

keyChanges.title: Copilot Chat in Outlook mobile gets refreshed navigation and prompts
keyChanges.detail: Outlook for iOS and Android will receive a refreshed Copilot Chat design with an improved chat interface, prompts, and navigation. Rollout starts in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late January 2027; no administrator action or compliance change is identified.

keyChanges.title: Classic Outlook receives visual consistency updates without workflow changes
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-November 2026, classic Outlook for Windows will update icons, spacing, and alignment. A nonintrusive monthly What’s New dialog will inform users, while the change does not alter workflows or replace the classic experience.

2026-11.headline: EWS replacement and Admin API changes lead November’s Exchange admin agenda
2026-11.overview: November’s consequential Exchange changes are operational rather than cosmetic. Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing are moving away from EWS to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy; Exchange Online Admin API permissions and a response contract are changing; and Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows will block additional file types by default. Updated hybrid guidance also narrows the supported OAuth migration environments and changes the required claim.
2026-11.adminImpact: Prioritize migration for affected cross-tenant EWS scenarios and inventory applications using the legacy Exchange Online Admin API permissions or the MailboxFolderPermission response. If users need .msix or .msixbundle attachments, allow those extensions in OwaMailboxPolicy before the December 2026 rollout. Hybrid administrators should align deployments with the updated Exchange prerequisites and xms_aud_guid claim, then test the migration endpoint and move-request commands.

keyChanges.title: Cross-tenant EWS scenarios move to Cross-Tenant Access Policy
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says EWS deprecation affects cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing from October 1, 2026. Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy is scheduled to replace EWS for these scenarios by late November 2026; GCC rollout is paused. Organizations using the affected workflows must migrate to avoid disruption.

keyChanges.title: Outlook adds .msix and .msixbundle to default blocked file types
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in December 2026, Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows will block .msix and .msixbundle by default through OwaMailboxPolicy. Organizations that need to receive or send these file types should allow them in the relevant policies before rollout.

keyChanges.title: Exchange Online Admin API permissions are being replaced
keyChanges.detail: Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 is replacing Exchange.ManageV2 and Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 with new permissions by November 2026. Affected applications need the replacement permissions, administrator consent, verified RBAC roles, testing, and removal of the legacy permissions to maintain access; endpoint changes are not expected.

keyChanges.title: MailboxFolderPermission changes User from a value to an object
keyChanges.detail: The Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 MailboxFolderPermission endpoint will return User as a structured object containing DisplayName, Name, and PrimarySmtpAddress by early November 2026. Applications consuming the endpoint must handle the new response shape to avoid errors.

keyChanges.title: OAuth migration endpoint guidance narrows hybrid prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: Updated OAuth Migration Endpoint guidance supports Microsoft 365 multi-tenant (WW) with on-premises Exchange Server Subscription Edition from October 2026 onward, or Exchange 2019 CU15 with the October 2026 security update. It changes the optional claim to xms_aud_guid and adds endpoint-testing and move-request examples; URI host values must match the migration commands.
